/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 06 October 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3002 (-68)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4638 (-195)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2366 (2)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1795 (5)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1005 (1)
CAPESIZE
The market opened the week on a busy note yesterday, despite a number of holidays in Asia, with brokers reporting up to about 10 fixtures or so on C5. Despite decent cargo volumes from both miners and operators, the market struggled to push higher and has since stabilised, with offers generally in the low to mid $14s. A miner was heard repeating last-done levels around $13.95 on a couple of occasions. Today, the C5 index edged up just 4 cents to $14.065, while C3 fell 83 cents to $36.027. In the Atlantic, conditions remained softer, with South Brazil and West Africa to China activity subdued and little in the way of meaningful bids or offers. Brokers are also reporting a growing ballaster list, while a softer transatlantic fixture saw C8 drop $6,281 to $48,563. Overall, the Pacific appears to be stabilising after recent weakness, although the Atlantic continues to face pressure. With three C5 miners active today and reasonable cargo volumes from both miners and operators, the Pacific feels more balanced, but there remains little evidence of a broader recovery.
PANAMAX
Reported fixture activity in the Atlantic improved today, with NC South America standing out as the most active area for trans-Atlantic rounds. Market participants described fundamentals as being fairly evenly balanced, although a wide bid-offer spread is still said to persist, particularly on fronthaul business. Sentiment remains positive overall, with owners reportedly holding firmer on their rate expectations. Market participants have noted that demand from EC South America remains relatively steady, with rates said to be heavily influenced by vessel arrival dates. Owners with October-loading positions are reportedly showing more resistance to current bid levels. Activity in the Pacific was reportedly slower today, which comes as little surprise given the ongoing holidays across the region. Demand from Australia and the North Pacific is said to remain evident, with some market participants suggesting that this is helping to keep fundamentals broadly balanced and, in turn, limiting any significant movement in the rates currently being discussed. The P5TC increased today by $21 to settle at $21,294.

Atlantic
The Crimson Kingdom (84,860 2016) open Ghent 7 October was reported fixed for a NC South America trans-Atlantic round with Bunge at $21,250. Meanwhile, Oldendorff were said to have placed the Thiseas (74,916 2011) open Gibraltar 11 October on subjects for similar business, with indications suggesting a rate in the region of $22,500 to $23,000. Elsewhere, Cofco were also heard to have covered their NC South America trans-Atlantic requirement, although no further details emerged.

Asia
The Primrose Atlantic (81,879 2016) Qinzhou 6/7 October fixed an EC Australia to Singapore-Japan range with coal at around $23,500 to $23,750 to Richland, while the scrubber-fitted Woolloomooloo (76,064 2012) open Guishan 9/10 October fixed for a similar trade at approximately $18,000. The Silvermine (77,230 2014) open Qingdao 12 October was heard on subjects with no further details reported, and Fullinks were linked with the Boyang Taurus (81,718 2016) open Bahodopi 12/13 October. Elsewhere, the Pelagia (82,178 2023) open Zhuhai mid/end October fixed an Indonesia to India coal stem at $22,000, while the Moon (80,505 2012) open Haldia 3 October secured an EC India coastal trip at $26,000.
SUPRAMAX
The quiet start to the week seemed to continue, but the 11TC average was up $64 to settle at $22,684, mainly due to the strength of the Pacific round voyage numbers. The AP Petka (63,619 2026) Mizushima 10-12 October was said to be on subjects to Dai An for a trip via NoPac to Bangladesh at a strong $27,000 and the Jabal Samhan (63,657 2015) fixed basis delivery Singapore about 11 October for a trip via Indonesia to India at $27,500, but no Charterer was mentioned. In the Atlantic sources said there was fresh demand in the US Gulf, which has stemmed the slide for the moment, and the south has managed to maintain levels despite ballasters from the Mediterranean prompting later stems to emerge in the market. The Continent remained firm but the Mediterranean was still subdued.
HANDYSIZE
The market showed a mixed tone today, with the 7TC average improving slightly by $28 to close at $18,095. Across the Continent and Mediterranean, only marginal changes were observed, and the market remained broadly balanced, with rates hovering around last-done levels across most loading areas. The South Atlantic saw a more active session, with several fixtures concluded and rates displaying a firmer tone. The Bahia (40,112 2017) was reported fixed for a trip from Upriver to the Continent in the low $30,000s, although further details were not disclosed. Meanwhile, the US Gulf was notably quiet, with limited reported activity and rates beginning to soften. The Pacific market recorded another slow day, as ongoing holidays across Asia continued to disrupt activity. Despite the subdued pace, rate levels remained relatively steady.

Market Fundamentals
Panama Canal Transit Slot Programme Extended

The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) announced it will extend its Long-term Slot Allocation (LoTSA) programme currently used for Neopanamax locks, to the Panamax locks, for the period 3 January to 3 April 2027. Slots will be allocated through sealed-bid auctions, with those for Neopanamax locks held on 17 November and the Panamax pilot auctions scheduled on 24 November. The Neopanamax programme offers 36 packages, totalling 270 slots (165 Northbound and 105 Southbound), while the Panamax programme offers 51 packages, totalling 288 slots (147 Northbound and 141 Southbound). Any remaining capacity remains to be offered through the standard reservation system and auctions. In the week ending 5 October, dry bulk transits through the Panama Canal stood at 1.3 Mdwt, up 0.4 Mdwt from the same time last year.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape was volatile but ultimately weaker, with the pressure concentrated in Oct. Oct started around 38,750–39,000, briefly traded up to 39,200, then sold off sharply through the day to 37,500 and eventually 37,000. Nov initially firmed from around 40,500 to 41,100 before reversing, trading down to 39,250–39,600 late. Q4 26 traded as high as 40,350 early before weakening to 38,650–39,100. FRESH ENQUIRY, PARTICULARLY OUT OF NCSA FOR MID-TO-END OCTOBER DATES, HAS HELPED IMPROVE THE SUPPLY-DEMAND BALANCE ACROSS THE BASIN. A FIRMER FFA MARKET THROUGH TUESDAY HAS ALSO ENCOURAGED OWNERS TO MAINTAIN HIGHER OFFERS, RESULTING IN WIDER BID-OFFER SPREADS. GENERAL TRADING HAS RANGED FROM AROUND $20,500 BKI EQUIVALENT TO $22,500 SUBJECT TO CARGO AND DURATION. OVERALL SENTIMENT IS RELATIVE...
